353.title: Customer History lists same-timestamp entries in a varying order
353.body:
Found while verifying #334 (PR #349); not part of that change.

**What happens**

A Customer's History tab lists entries that share a timestamp in a different order from one load to the next. During the #334 run, two loads of the same Customer showed the same entries in a different order, on `pre-main` and on the #349 branch alike.

**Evidence**

The tab reads `python3 -m ledger history` → `AuditStore.list_by_entity` in `ledger/audit_store.py`, which orders by `changed_at DESC` only. Each audit service call stamps all field rows of one Audit Operation with the same `changed_at`, so the rows of one operation (and of operations landing on the same instant) have no defined order and the database may return them differently each time. The paginated list behind the Audit Log (`AuditStore.list` in the same file) already breaks ties on `entity_type, entity_id, action, changed_by, field_name`, so it does not show this.

Related, in the same query: `LIMIT` counts field rows, not Audit Operations, so with more than the limit (default 50) an operation can be cut off part-way and show fewer fields than it changed. Not observed; noted for triage.

**Impact**

The owner sees the field changes of one edit shuffle between views of the same Customer, which makes the history harder to read and compare.
353.author: owner

comments.author: owner
comments.body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

Triage checks: premise still holds on `origin/pre-main`: `list_by_entity` orders by `changed_at DESC` only, while `list` breaks ties on the operation key and `field_name`. No open issue covers the same query; no `.out-of-scope/` entry. Confirmed by code path. The `LIMIT`-counts-field-rows part is split into #376, so this issue is the order only.

## Agent Brief

**Category:** bug
**Summary:** Customer History lists the rows of one Audit Operation in a stable order

**Current behavior:**
The per-entity history query (`AuditStore.list_by_entity`, used by the Customer History tab) orders by `changed_at` descending only. All field rows of one Audit Operation share a `changed_at`, so their order is undefined and can change between loads.

**Desired behavior:**
`list_by_entity` returns rows in the same order the Audit Log list (`AuditStore.list`) uses: newest operation first, ties between operations broken on `action` and `changed_by`, and within one operation the field rows by `field_name` ascending. Two loads of the same Customer list the same rows in the same order.

**Key interfaces:**
- `AuditStore.list_by_entity(entity_type, entity_id, limit)`: return shape unchanged, only the order is defined

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] A test writes one multi-field operation with its rows inserted out of `field_name` order and asserts `list_by_entity` returns them by `field_name`; it fails on the pre-fix query
- [ ] Operations at different times still come newest first
- [ ] `python3 -m ledger history` shows a multi-field edit's rows in `field_name` order

**Out of scope:**
- Paging by operation instead of by row (#376)
- The `list` query and the Audit Log

376.title: Paginate Customer History by Audit Operation, not by row

comments.author: owner
comments.body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

Triage checks: premise holds on `origin/pre-main`: `list_by_entity` ends in `LIMIT ?` on field rows, so an Audit Operation with more fields than the room left is cut off part-way. No open issue covers paging; #353 covers the order only.

## Agent Brief

**Category:** enhancement
**Summary:** Customer History pages by Audit Operation, so an operation is never cut off part-way

**Current behavior:**
`AuditStore.list_by_entity(entity_type, entity_id, limit)` applies `LIMIT` to field rows. With more rows than `limit`, the last operation shown can lose some of its fields.

**Desired behavior:**
`limit` counts Audit Operations: `list_by_entity` returns every field row of the entity's newest `limit` operations, and no row of an older one. An Audit Operation is the rows of one entity that share `changed_at`, `action` and `changed_by`.

**Key interfaces:**
- `AuditStore.list_by_entity(entity_type, entity_id, limit)`: same signature and row shape; `limit` (default 50) now counts operations

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] A test writes three operations of one, three and two fields and asserts `list_by_entity(..., limit=2)` returns the five rows of the two newest; it fails on the pre-fix query
- [ ] Another entity's rows never count toward the limit

**Out of scope:**
- The order of rows within an operation (#353)
- The Audit Log page (`AuditStore.list`)

376.body: Split from #353: `LIMIT` in `AuditStore.list_by_entity` counts field rows, so an operation can be cut off part-way.
